likely_trigger: Before the open on Oct 16 Omeros announced that the EMA's CHMP had maintained its negative opinion on the narsoplimab (YARTEMLEA) marketing authorization application in TA-TMA after re-examination, and that it would end its European compassionate-use program.

trigger_source.title: Omeros Corporation Receives CHMP Negative Opinion Following Re-Examination of European Marketing Authorization Application for Narsoplimab in TA-TMA
trigger_source.publisher: Omeros Corporation (press release via Business Wire; retrieved from Benzinga on Bigdata.com)

trigger_quote: Omeros Corporation (NASDAQ:OMER) today announced that the Committee for Medicinal Products for Human Use (CHMP) of the European Medicines Agency (EMA) issued a negative opinion on the company's marketing authorization application (MAA) for narsoplimab for the treatment of hematopoietic stem cell transplant-associated thrombotic microangiopathy (TA-TMA) following re-examination of its original negative opinion adopted in June 2026.
tier_reason: Regulatory failure on the company's lead product after the company stated it believed the evidence supported approval (trigger-tiers: 'Clinical trial, regulatory or product failure after confident statements'). Caveat: the original negative opinion (June 2026) was already public, so this is the re-examination outcome of a known setback.

alternatives.explanation: CHMP negative opinion after re-examination (company press release before the open)
alternatives.why: Timed before the open (Benzinga 10:20Z; MT Newswires 11:08Z shows -2.6% pre-market); multiple outlets attribute the 14% fall to it. Peers flat (+0.03%); abnormal -13.6%, t -4.70; volume 3.05x average (script).

alternatives.explanation: Termination of the European compassionate-use program, announced in the same release
alternatives.why: Same document, same time; cannot be separated from the CHMP news at daily frequency.
IBB -2.6% late Friday (MT Newswires), but the script's peer return was +0.03% and expected return -0.2%.

prior_statement_check.quote: We believe the clinical evidence supports approval and have requested re-examination. [...] although there can be no guarantee that the re-examination will result in a reversal of CHMP's negative opinion or the ultimate approval of the MAA.

source.title: Omeros Corp Form 10-Q for the quarter ended June 30, 2026
source.location: Business overview, YARTEMLEA / European MAA paragraph (Bigdata.com doc EB3E04F66B18566C5DB2DE98B829D579, chunks 20 and 104)

prior_statement_check.note: Mixed: the company expressed belief that the evidence supports approval (same wording in the Aug 12, 2026 earnings release, 8-K Ex. 99.1) but expressly cautioned that re-examination might not reverse the opinion; the June 2026 negative opinion itself was disclosed when made. Classified 'warned specifically' because the specific risk (no reversal on re-examination) was stated before the drop. EDGAR full-text search for "re-examination" (CIK 1285819, 2024-10-16..2026-10-15) returned 5 filings: 8-K Ex.99.1 and 10-Q of 2026-08-12, ARS 2025-05-30, 10-Ks of 2025-03-31 and 2026-03-31 - not opened beyond the 10-Q excerpt. Layer 2 should check what the company said about the AHEG process and patient-level data, since the release now says CHMP did not provide that data to the AHEG.
